english: Let $F:(-3,3)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that $F(0)=0$ and $F'(x)=\dfrac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{9-x^{2}}}$ for all $x\in(-3,3)$. Let $\theta$ be the angle with $-90^{\circ}<\theta<90^{\circ}$ such that $F(3\sin\theta)=\dfrac{9\sqrt2}{8}-\dfrac{9\pi}{16}$. If $\theta$ is measured in degrees, then the value of $\theta$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $F:(-3,3)\to\mathbb{R}$ एक अवकलनीय फलन है जिसके लिए $F(0)=0$ तथा सभी $x\in(-3,3)$ के लिए $F'(x)=\dfrac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{9-x^{2}}}$ है। माना कि $\theta$ वह कोण है जिसके लिए $-90^{\circ}<\theta<90^{\circ}$ तथा $F(3\sin\theta)=\dfrac{9\sqrt2}{8}-\dfrac{9\pi}{16}$ है। यदि $\theta$ को अंशों (degrees) में मापा जाए, तो $\theta$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $F'\geq0$ and $3\sin\phi$ is increasing, so $\phi\mapsto F(3\sin\phi)$ is strictly increasing: at most one solution
solution_full: Use the substitution $x=3\sin\phi$ with $\phi\in\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ measured in radians (calculus formulas require radians). Then $\cos\phi>0$, $\sqrt{9-x^{2}}=3\cos\phi$ and $dx=3\cos\phi\,d\phi$.

Integrating: $\dfrac92\phi-\dfrac94\sin2\phi+C$. Since $F(0)=0$ corresponds to $\phi=0$, $C=0$ and $F(3\sin\phi)=\dfrac92\phi-\dfrac94\sin2\phi$. (Geometrically, $\dfrac92\cdot2\phi$ is the area of a sector of radius $3$ and angle $2\phi$, so $F$ is half a sector minus a triangle.)

Uniqueness: $F'(x)\geq0$ with equality only at $x=0$, so $F$ is strictly increasing; $\phi\mapsto3\sin\phi$ is strictly increasing, so the composition is strictly increasing and the equation has at most one root.

Compare $\dfrac92\phi-\dfrac94\sin2\phi$ with $-\dfrac{9\pi}{16}+\dfrac{9\sqrt2}{8}$: the choice $\phi=-\dfrac{\pi}{8}$ gives $\dfrac92\phi=-\dfrac{9\pi}{16}$ and $\sin2\phi=\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=-\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$, so $-\dfrac94\sin2\phi=\dfrac{9\sqrt2}{8}$. It is a root, hence the only one.
originality_note: New: the antiderivative of x^2/sqrt(9-x^2) is read in the angle variable (half a sector minus a triangle), and the angle at which it takes a given value is asked in degrees, so the radian result of the trigonometric substitution must be converted (way 5). Closest known: integral of x^2/sqrt(a^2-x^2) by x = a sin(theta). Different because: the question inverts the antiderivative, needs a monotonicity argument for uniqueness, and asks for a degree measure.
key_step: Substituting x = 3 sin(theta) to get (9/2)theta - (9/4) sin 2theta, matching the given value at theta = -pi/8 with uniqueness, and converting to degrees.
justification: Trigonometric substitution plus an inverse step (matching a value, with a monotonicity check) and a units conversion, with no options. Two ideas linked; comparable to 2024-P2-Q16 (L2) circle-area integral raised one level by the inversion and numerical format, near 2023-P2-Q8 (L3).
blueprint_concepts: Measurement of angles: degree, radian, arc length and sector area

concept_use.Integration by trigonometric substitutio: The substitution x = 3 sin(theta) turns x^2/sqrt(9-x^2) dx into 9 sin^2(theta) d(theta), integrated by power reduction.
concept_use.Measurement of angles: degree, radian, a: The angle found in radians (-pi/8) is converted to degrees (-22.5); the antiderivative is half a sector area of radius 3 minus a triangle, which is why radian measure is required.
